questions.tag: United States of America · Fixed income
questions.q: What is bitcoin, in the context of financial markets?
o: A digital asset that acts as an alternative store of value
A government-issued currency managed by a central bank
A physical precious metal traded in standard bullion bars
A debt security issued by the federal government
questions.e: Bitcoin is a digital asset or cryptocurrency that is compared to gold as an alternative store of value. Unlike government debt securities or traditional currencies, it exists purely in digital form and trades with varying sensitivity to yield movements.

questions.tag: United States of America · Fixed income
questions.q: What is inflation?
o: The rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services rises
The total amount of money borrowed by a national government
The interest paid by the government on bonds over a year
The profit earned by a technology company from artificial intelligence
questions.e: Inflation measures how fast prices are increasing across the economy. Central banks watch it closely because rising prices erode purchasing power and influence interest rate decisions.

questions.q: What are gilts?
o: Bonds issued by the British government to borrow money
Shares of companies that trade on the London Stock Exchange
Tax payments collected by the treasury from corporate profits
Emergency funds held by commercial banks for lending
questions.e: Gilts are bonds issued by the UK government. When the government needs to borrow, it sells gilts to investors, promising to pay them back with interest over time.

questions.q: What happens when a company is removed from the FTSE 100 index?
o: Funds that track the index are forced to sell their holdings of its shares
The company is immediately banned from trading on public stock exchanges
The government takes over the management of the firm's debt
Its stock price automatically rises due to increased retail demand
questions.e: Index reclassification means funds that mechanically copy the FTSE 100 must adjust their portfolios by selling the demoted company's shares. This mandatory adjustment comes from index-tracking rules rather than corporate earnings performance.

questions.q: What is a stock index like the DAX?
o: A statistical measure of the value of a group of important companies
An agreement to buy crude oil at a fixed price in the future
A loan provided by the European Central Bank to commercial banks
A measure of total national economic output over a quarter
questions.e: The DAX is an index tracking a group of major German companies. When the index moves down, it means the overall value of those grouped equities has fallen.

questions.q: What does a central bank do when it sets interest rates?
o: It influences the cost of borrowing money throughout the economy
It dictates the daily share price of major energy corporations
It buys and sells physical barrels of crude oil in commodity markets
It sets the tax rates that corporations pay to the government
questions.e: The European Central Bank sets monetary policy and interest rates. Changes in these rates affect borrowing costs for businesses and consumers across the continent.

questions.q: What does it mean when a currency like the Japanese yen rises against the US dollar?
o: Each unit of the yen buys more US dollars than before
The Japanese government has lowered its domestic tax rates
The total volume of goods imported into Japan has decreased
The interest rate paid on Japanese government bonds has fallen to zero
questions.e: A currency appreciating or surging means it gains value relative to another currency. A stronger yen buys more greenbacks because traders expect higher interest rates in Japan.

questions.q: Why would a government inject money into state banks and insurers?
o: To support them during periods when overall economic growth is slowing
To punish them for failing to meet international lending standards
To replace all physical currency with digital tokens immediately
To finance the construction of new artificial intelligence hardware factories
questions.e: Governments provide capital injections to financial institutions to shore up their balance sheets. In China, this funding was deployed as economic growth slowed down.

questions.q: What is a central bank doing when it increases its gold reserves for many consecutive months?

It is selling bullion to lower the global market price of gold
It is using gold coins to pay off foreign government debt directly
It is minting new currency backed entirely by consumer electronics
questions.e: A central bank increasing its gold holdings is systematically buying and storing bullion. This continuous accumulation builds up the official reserve assets held by the monetary authority.

questions.q: How does a surge in crude oil prices typically affect an oil-importing country's currency?

It strengthens the local currency by boosting domestic oil production revenues
It has no impact because oil is purchased using local currency reserves
It causes the currency to appreciate as foreign investors buy local bonds
questions.e: When oil prices surge, an importing nation needs more foreign currency to pay for its energy imports. This increased demand for foreign exchange puts downward pressure on the local currency like the rupee.

questions.q: What is an FPSO in the context of offshore oil production?

A fixed pipeline running along the ocean floor to refineries
A deepwater submarine used to lay underwater electrical cables
A shore-based facility that refines crude oil into gasoline
questions.e: An FPSO is a floating production, storage and offloading vessel. These units operate offshore to extract and process petroleum from deepwater wells before transferring it to tankers.

questions.q: What is the purpose of OPEC+ setting output targets for its member nations?

To set the retail price of gasoline in local service stations
To eliminate the need for oil refineries in member countries
To transition all member economies away from fossil fuel extraction
questions.e: OPEC+ is a group of oil-producing countries that agrees on output quotas. By coordinating extraction volumes, these nations attempt to manage global supply and maintain market stability.

questions.q: What does a growing foreign exchange reserve enable a central bank to do?

It allows the government to abolish all taxes on corporate profits

questions.e: Foreign exchange reserves are foreign currencies held by a central bank. Large reserves give the central bank the financial capacity to intervene in markets and support the local currency's value.

The official interest rate charged by the central bank to commercial banks

questions.q: How can gross domestic product and inflation figures influence a central bank's interest rate decisions?
